principle_violations.reason: The AreaCalculator class has multiple responsibilities: calculating the area of shapes and producing output, violating SRP.
principle_violations.suggestion: Separate the area calculation and the output generation into different classes. This can be achieved by creating an OutputManager class that handles formatting output.

suggestion_code: public double getAreaSum() { return sum(); } // New method to get area sum
public String output(double areaSum) { return "Sum of the areas of provided shapes: " + areaSum; }

principle_violations.reason: The AreaCalculator class needs to be modified to support new shape types. This violates the Open/Closed Principle as adding a new shape will require changes in the existing code.
principle_violations.suggestion: Introduce a Shape interface with a method for calculating the area, and make Circle and Square implement this interface. This allows new shapes to be added without modifying existing calculations.

principle_violations.reason: The AreaCalculator class depends on a generic List<Object>, which forces it to work with shapes it does not expect to handle. This violates the ISP.
principle_violations.suggestion: Change the AreaCalculator to depend on a List<Shape> instead of List<Object> to ensure it only operates on objects of type Shape.

overall_feedback: 3 principle violations found. Please see the details below.
